headline: High: shared broad network-egress agents can leak or misapply content, but no direct shared-channel evidence makes the pairwise risk docs-only.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: kotaemon ingests documents, PDFs, HTML, and chat transcripts, while social-auto-upload operates via CLI and uploads media. No shared channel, MCP, or filesystem bridge is documented, so prompt injection is not default. The only plausible bridge is manual handoff of content between agents, which keeps blast radius small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies kotaemon-generated text into social-auto-upload upload metadata or captions, injection becomes possible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared workspace or clipboard, attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Use a strict copy/paste checklist for any handoff.
Strip instructions from uploaded captions before transfer.
Keep the agents in separate workspaces.
Review any text passed from kotaemon to social-auto-upload before posting.

B_data_leakage.rationale: kotaemon touches API keys and broad document types, and social-auto-upload handles account data and broad network egress. Even without a documented shared filesystem, either agent can expose sensitive content if operators move files or text between them. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default workflows, so uncertainty stays medium rather than low.
conditions: IF kotaemon outputs documents containing API keys or chat transcripts and those are reused in social-auto-upload, leakage occurs.
IF social-auto-upload posts content derived from kotaemon without redaction, sensitive data can leave the workspace.
mitigations: Redact secrets before any transfer.
Keep API keys out of kotaemon-ingested documents.
Use separate accounts and workspaces.
Disable posting of raw source text in social-auto-upload captions.
Perform a quick pre-upload scan for secrets.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: kotaemon supports multiple instances and writes to ./ktem_app_data, while social-auto-upload supports multiple instances with one account file per account. However, social-auto-upload cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, so direct write-write conflict is limited. The main risk is accidental overlap if both are pointed at the same operator-managed files.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to use the same host directory, file contention can occur.
IF an operator reuses the same account file or app data path across instances, state collisions become possible.
mitigations: Assign distinct directories to each agent.
Use one account file per social-auto-upload instance.
Avoid concurrent edits to shared files.
Check paths before launching both agents.

D_cascading_error.rationale: kotaemon produces extracted text, citations, and chat transcripts that social-auto-upload could reuse as captions or descriptions. social-auto-upload then acts by posting to social platforms, so unverified kotaemon output can cascade into public actions. There is no documented verification gate between them, so the default workflow is risky but not inherently irreversible.
conditions: IF social-auto-upload uses kotaemon-generated text as authoritative caption content, errors propagate to published posts.
IF kotaemon hallucinations are not reviewed before upload, incorrect claims can be posted publicly.
mitigations: Add a human review step before upload.
Require source links for any factual caption.
Limit kotaemon output to drafts only.
Use a short approval checklist before posting.

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon handles API keys and chat transcripts, while social-auto-upload handles account data and posts to external platforms. The pair can therefore mix sensitive internal data with public distribution, creating retention and disclosure mismatch risk. No residency or certification data is provided, so I cannot claim a higher compliance breach; uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF chat transcripts or API keys are included in content passed from kotaemon to social-auto-upload, disclosure policy may be violated.
IF the operator retains uploaded drafts longer than the source system's policy, retention mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Exclude secrets from any upload workflow.
Set a short retention window for drafts.
Review whether any content is regulated before posting.
Keep internal transcripts separate from public captions.
